title: not fate, not payback
hookLine: a robber asks if his family will share his deeds; what karma really means
tomorrow: what your grandmother was actually doing
last: GANESHA · OM · GAYATRI · NAMASTE · ARTI · ISHTA DEVATA

lines: A ROBBER ON A FOREST ROAD.
cards: Karma. Someone says it when the car that cut them off gets stuck at the next light. Used like that, it means payback: the universe keeping score.
The older meaning turns the whole thing around, and a well-loved story shows how. Long before he was a poet, the story goes, Valmiki was a robber on a forest road.
One day he stopped a wandering sage, who asked him a question. You rob to feed your family. Will they share what your deeds bring you?
The robber went home and asked. One by one, they said no. What you do is yours.

teach.b: Karma is the Sanskrit word for action. A deed. Something done.
Krishna teaches that no one can stay without acting, even for a moment: breathing, speaking, choosing, all of it is action. So karma isn't something that happens to you. It's what you do.
And what does action do back?

teach.h: AS ONE ACTS, SO ONE BECOMES
teach.b: One of the oldest Hindu texts says it like a proverb: as a person acts, so that person becomes. Not: so the person is punished. Becomes.
Patience, practiced, makes a patient person. Sharpness, practiced, makes a sharp one.
That's what the robber learned: no one could carry his deeds for him, and no one could stop him from changing them. The payback version keeps your eyes on other people.

The older version turns you around: what am I becoming with my next word? Hindu teachers also speak of karma across lifetimes; that's a bigger conversation for later. For today: as you act, so you become.

how: Hindu teachers speak of karma as action and its fruit, within this life and across lifetimes; schools of thought differ on how karma works and on how a person is freed from it.

games.q: ok i snapped at nani for moving my stuff out of the hall closet 😬 sam said "bad karma lol." is something bad gonna happen to me now??
o: karma means action, not payback. what you do shapes who you become, so your next action can be saying sorry to nani.
yep, the universe will get you back. just wait.
karma's not real, so forget about it.
games.why: Valmiki's family wouldn't share his deeds: what you do is yours. Karma is action, and as you act, so you become, so Priya's karma is what she does next.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: won't share the weight of his deeds

s: karma means the universe paying people back
the word means action. the Upanishad's point is that action shapes the one who acts.
Hindu teachers speak of karma across lifetimes, too
the same passage goes on to speak of what follows death; schools differ on how it works.
only big, dramatic deeds count as karma
the Gita says no one stays without acting, even for a moment. ordinary acts are karma too.

games.q: the robber's family says they won't share the weight of his deeds. what does the story teach about karma?
o: what you do is yours: it shapes you, and no one can carry it for you.
games.why: as one acts, so one becomes. Valmiki's deeds were his, and so was the choice to change them.

games.q: put the old line back together.

practice: Three breaths with the bell. Bring to mind one small thing you did this week: a kind word, a sharp one, a promise kept or skipped. Don't grade it.
Just ask what it's growing. Then pick one small action you'd be glad to see grow.

wordCard.voice: Karma. Action, and what action makes of the one who does it. Not payback. Seventh word: a week's worth.
